summary:
Seven Sols is an interactive Mars mission training game developed by Team Kayseri Mantıları for children aged 7–12 as part of NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

Instead of simply memorizing facts about space, players explore a Martian outpost, complete missions, and manage four essential resources: energy, oxygen, food, and radiation shielding. Every decision involves trade-offs, encouraging players to think about how protecting one system can affect another.

Inspired by NASA/JPL’s InSight mission observations of declining solar power generation on Mars, Seven Sols connects real scientific challenges with simplified, age-appropriate gameplay.

Our goal is to introduce young learners to sustainability, engineering decisions, resource management, and systems thinking through interactive exploration and meaningful consequences.
details:
The Problem

Many children learn facts about space exploration without experiencing the engineering decisions behind real missions. Astronauts and mission planners must manage limited resources, respond to unexpected challenges, and consider how one decision affects other systems.

Our Solution

Seven Sols is an interactive, browser-based Mars outpost mission trainer designed for children aged 7–12. It turns complex engineering challenges into understandable gameplay.

Instead of simply answering trivia questions, players explore a fictional Martian outpost, interact with stations, complete mini-games, and make resource-management decisions.

How the Game Works

Players control an astronaut, explore the outpost, follow guidance from ARES, and complete mission activities as the Martian sols progress.

The mission revolves around four interconnected resources:

  • Energy: Powers essential outpost systems.
  • Oxygen: Represents life-support needs.
  • Food: Supports mission sustainability.
  • Radiation Shielding: Represents protection against radiation hazards.

Players must balance these resources rather than maximize one resource independently.

For example, the Shield Generator offers two maintenance options:

  • Standard Maintenance: +15 Shield, −10 Energy.
  • Energy-Saving Maintenance: +9 Shield, −5 Energy.

Standard maintenance provides more protection but consumes more energy. Energy-saving maintenance conserves power but provides less shielding.

Neither option is always correct. The appropriate decision depends on the current mission conditions.

Scientific Foundation

During development, our team researched NASA/JPL’s InSight mission and its historical solar-energy observations.

InSight’s solar power production decreased from approximately 5,000 Wh per Martian day after landing to approximately 500 Wh per Martian day by spring 2022.

We adapted this scientific observation into a simplified energy-management mechanic to help players understand how environmental conditions can affect mission sustainability.

The game’s resource points are fictional educational units, not real spacecraft measurements.

Technology and Creativity

Seven Sols was developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and browser-based graphics technologies.

The project combines exploration, interactive station activities, mission progression, and interconnected resource decisions.

Serdar Ege AKER served as Team Leader and Lead Developer, taking primary responsibility for programming, visual development, project coordination, and submission preparation.

The other four team members provided occasional ideas and general support.

OpenAI ChatGPT/Codex assisted with programming, debugging, interface development, visual elements, and narrative content.

Educational Purpose and Impact

Our goal is to introduce children to engineering trade-offs, sustainability, mission planning, and systems thinking.

By observing the consequences of their choices, players can explore why space missions require careful planning and compromise.

Seven Sols is intended to encourage curiosity, experimentation, and problem-solving.

Limitations and Future Development

Seven Sols is an educational prototype rather than a professional astronaut training simulator.

It does not reproduce actual spacecraft engineering calculations or use live NASA telemetry.

Formal classroom validation and measured educational outcomes have not yet been completed.

Future development could include improved accessibility, additional NASA-based mission scenarios, teacher-guided activities, and structured learning evaluations.

Last 48 Hours — Team Kayseri Mantıları

Our story started with a simple idea: What if kids could do more than just read about Mars? What if they could experience the difficult decisions themselves? That’s how Seven Sols began.

Serdar Ege led the development, turning his ideas into a playable Mars outpost game with the help of ChatGPT and Codex. Our teammates supported the project by testing the game and reviewing our presentation. Mehmet even completed the game twice, sharing feedback on the visual effects and gameplay.

During our final 48 hours, we faced an unexpected problem: we accidentally deleted our source code! Thankfully, we managed to recover it and create a backup.

This journey taught us patience, teamwork, and the importance of finding solutions when things go wrong.

Most importantly, we created a game where children can experience the challenge of balancing limited resources like energy, oxygen, food, and radiation protection on Mars.
